notes.title: Media Player!!!
notes.content:
[p]Hey!

This week I have been working on a media player for the JAMs songs, and I think I've got it pretty much complete at this point, or usable at least.  I made a bunch of AI music like a year ago, and I stopped working on that since the game itself was so far from complete at the time.  Now that the game is starting to get more complete, the next logical step was to add the music in.  [b][i]The prophecy is complete[/i] --- JAMs now [u]actually[/u] has JAMs in it!!![/b]  [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45270362/77ddb2bb26ad8dee4d665f625b4b298004be14b7.png"][/img][/p][p]When you don't want it open, you can just minimize it using the 'X' on the end there:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45270362/cd5ed4510e9c767204a913edb7e1409b0a5bc5a9.png"][/img][/p][p]Click on this 'Song List' button to view your songs:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45270362/cc8f6d672ef69d8575fa257986aca2872818be38.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45270362/e5dff8414078f398a11a76ec04cb8052f9be2c35.png"][/img][/p][p]And your playlist screen might look something like this.  The songs are locked behind items, so you may have a ridiculous sounding playlist if you only have 1 item with a song in it, but I only added like 27 songs in there so far.  I haven't made any music for awhile so I have to get back into that zone one of these days!  At least the system will exist from a technical perspective with a few songs and I can add them in over time.  I could also include some of those tracks from the royalty-free BGM music packs from bundles if they have any good songs, I have quite a few of those to go through.[/p][p]I was trying to think of how to categorize the items from an inventory tagging perspective, for now what I have done is put a music note and the track name in the item description (that's how I made the system detect them).  I might need to come up with a bit more granular of a tag for the genre of the music, I am just thinking eventually if you have thousands of songs and they are a total random mix of rap, country, & electronic, a button to change the genre could work like a radio station.  [/p][p]At the moment, the system gives you 2 playlists: [b]Game[/b] and [b]Menu[/b]. You can have a different set of songs enabled for when you are on the menu or playing a game.  That should work for a version 1 for now, you can at least disable songs.  [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45270362/3f79fa214f88a0f5e92997166d97264f5f059597.png"][/img][/p][p]Oh and if you click this button in the settings menu, you can change the media player's position (pinned to top or bottom of the window).  To change the volume, use the volume control in the settings menu for music.[/p]

notes.title: New JAMTRIS MiniGame!
notes.content:
[p]Okay I spent a few days wrestling with Unity but I finally got it done --- the first minigame [i][b]JAMTRIS[/b][/i] is complete!  You can access it via this icon on the main screen for now:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45270362/51e4de9308de7c056e7e7d56eaed1d760f9ac929.png"][/img][/p][p]So in the minigame when you score points, [u][b]it immediately counts towards your click counter on the main screen[/b][/u], so technically you could just play this game [i]INSTEAD[/i] of active clicking, and the auto-clicker [i](if equipped) [/i]will still be clicking away in the background.  The points/steamstat are awarded per-line-clear (not at the game-over screen, when the high score is submitted).   to just give you another way to advance towards those achievements.  I didn't add an achievement yet for JAMTRIS, if I do I'll make it very reasonable to hit, like maybe a score of 10K...  I can't make the minigames each really hard to complete if I add lots of them, so don't worry about a huge score requirement from this.  The points double for each level you advance to (each 10 lines cleared advances the level).[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45270362/8bbc9ddb992c1fd7aebb09287a9277c56f5cc73e.jpg"][/img][/p][p]I have also started working on the leaderboards.  You will see Unique Items Owned, Clicks, Time Played JAMTRIS score all starting to accumulate on the Steam Community tab now.  I will get the leaderboard displays inside of the game ready in the next day or two![/p][p]Also the gamepad controls for JAMTRIS are ready to go, if you have a controller it works great![/p][p]Now future minigames will be a lot easier to program in too, it took some time trying to get game-world objects into a 2D UI, but now that little background panel itself is a RenderTexture that displays a game, we can technically put any kind of 3D games to be played inside the existing JAMs UI.  [/p][p]A lot of restructuring took place so I hopefully have fixed most of everything that broke in the process.  I can already see a bug with tooltips showing up too wide for the game UI now... and background color doesn't update until you flip the scene --- expect a few tiny bugs like that right now, I'm super glad it's at least 99% back together again anyway![/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45270362/81d65c14ee8e5488f1f224677471cafe2010ab6d.png"][/img][/p]

notes.title: New collection screen
notes.content: [p]Hey I added a new collection screen to the app, it's located to the far left![/p][p]You can click on the items you own and you will be taken to the item details screen for that item.  It also shows the quantity of that item in the list!  [/p][p]You can change the sort order to be ID# and by name, and I made it display that text in your chosen language.  [/p][p]The 'back' button on the item details screen will go to the inventory if you click in from there, but if you click in from the collection screen, the back button will go back to collection (and the hover tooltip displaying correctly).  [/p][p]I might tweak the visual design of this screen a bit more (the green on owned items is a bit jarring) but for now it seems to work pretty good! You can use this to quickly navigate to a certain item without using the inventory screen at all.[/p][p]There may be a few extra at the bottom that are unreleased / WIP items, ignore those for now.  I'll have to optimize my search filter without having to build-in a set item # into the game to end at.  If I leave the descriptions as 'TBD' it will ignore those so I can just leave the descriptions as that until they are almost ready to launch.[/p][p]I also made it so the items in the collection screen not yet owned are clickable and go to the corresponding Steam Market page instead of the item details screen, and on the item details screen there is now an icon to go to the Steam Market page for that item.  The ones that are unmarketable don't have these links.  [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45270362/b3544e1b2e751ce984f85ac566a4666b3bf0a46c.png"][/img][/p]

notes.title: Optimized Inventory Screen
notes.content:
[p]Hey!  Quick update here, I know the inventory screen is a bit of a chore to use with all the images it has to load, so I did some tweaks.  I created a new mode that has memory management, and I made it remember what page you are on when you are browsing through the items.  [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45270362/dddf92ac5b919ddf898e3559624c74853848340b.png"][/img]
[i]When you click the back button, it remembers what page you were browsing.[/i][/p][p]This new mode is now the default, and I removed the mode selector toggle.  Now the game can stay under 2-3GB of RAM as you browse through the pages.  There may still be a tiny memory leak but it's very manageable now compared to before.  [/p][p]It can have some strange appearance sometimes (items appearing twice as they download in, white squares etc) but it's worth it for the memory savings, I'll try clean up the screen a bit more down the road.  [/p]

notes.title: Crafting Update!
notes.content: [p]Hello everyone!  I've been grinding away on this for awhile and I've finally got it working.  I created a way to exchange your items for a Silver & Gold currency, and this will be used for features within the game and also it would be cool to have minigames where you could earn more silver too.  [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45270362/ef281269b7d6f3da64e324845018c9b9c91df8b3.png"][/img][/p][p][i]The button to exchange items is on the details screen for each item.[/i][/p][p]Each common (or DLC) type item can be exchanged for 1 silver, and 100 silvers will automatically convert into 1 gold.  Each 'rare' can be exchanged for 1 gold each.  You can do them in bulk in 1x, 10x, or 100x multipliers by right-clicking on the exchange button to toggle your quantity.  By default, it expects your items to be stacked.  If they are all loose, there's a toggle switch in the settings to try craft in bulk with the loose items.   [/p][p]I imagine creating a little shop inside the game where you can spend the gold on different items, but for now it's purpose is to give you an extra boost on your click counter to work toward the achievements.  Each gold can be spent to gain 1 million clicks onto your click counter instantly.  This will help people find more of a purpose to the items if they don't want them and also make the items rarer if people are trading in their inventories into the achievement progress boost.    [/p][p]It's not 100% perfect, but I'm still kind of tweaking the UI aspect.  If your quantities get slightly out of sync, they will just fix themselves after a few minutes or as you move around in the program.  I think we still need a switch to keep 1 of each item (currently it will take your last one, expect a settings toggle coming) and there is no confirmation dialog or anything to prevent mistakes.  I still need to make the inventory operate a bit faster, but was focused purely on making this crafting work all week and it's finally ready for you guys to try.  Now that crafting works, I can then create replacement items for the original ~16 items with broken descriptions too, that's coming sooner than later now.  Each unmarketable item will have a replacement marketable version to swap into, and then also swap back into the old versions too (since they would come out with proper descriptions in the craft).    [/p][p]Lots to do!  Let me know if you are experiencing any issues with it.[/p]

notes.title: Use your items as the clicking button!
notes.content:
[p]Hey!  I am building the screen to view details about the items in inventory, and it's shaping up pretty well!  
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45270362/a960f8b3e5abd0f0bfe5fcda7cb942c87edfde5a.png"][/img][/p][p]You can click the heart icon on the item details screen of an item to add that item to be your favorite, and it will replace your clicking button on the main screen.  Click favorite again on the same item to disable it.    [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45270362/d8fa0f1aede96f9eaf7a4e04962d80727e8fd934.png"][/img][/p][p]I'll be adding more stats and buttons onto this details screen too.  

[b]You can use the left/right arrows to navigate to the next items you own[/b], and it will download the primary image for that item as needed.  Things load faster once they get cached.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45270362/87e561e3d10f6ab3b4a6ea6fcacbe06028680276.png"][/img] [/p][p]The inventory screen itself is [i]still[/i] really heavy, we could use a more basic text-based version or a different mode on the existing one, like loading static images of each in inventory and then animate them as you hover, but we'll worry about that later.  I didn't make any changes to the inventory screen recently, but I just wanted to add a reminder about this button here in the settings and how it is fairly important at the moment.  People with few item types will probably barely notice a difference, this is for those who have tons of different items.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45270362/855702d264fe5074c7d4be98bc7416feeb8c553e.png"][/img] [/p][p]Currently they way it works is inventory mode 1 will pre-load your entire inventory (uses tons of RAM, takes a long time, but pages turn instantly when loaded) and mode 2 will load the items one page at a time.  [u]You should basically always be using mode 2 for inventory[/u] but it can be slow to skip through 20 pages that way so you may still need the preload mode sometimes, for example if you wanted to let it load for a few minutes then quickly browse the pages to the item you want without any delays.  [/p][p]At the moment loading my inventory in mode 2 on the first page causes the system to use 2GB of RAM:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45270362/e07b7f63c5cc840842c1e3d043a8e570e3df4f5e.png"][/img][/p][p]And then using mode 1 (with 348 unique items) it will use over 30GB of RAM:

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45270362/40fa682ae516ac45a846ca46612ec26addc8bf52.png"][/img][/p][p]Which obviously is not ideal, especially as more items get released..  And when you use mode 2, it is a lot lighter but it still eats more memory up as you go deeper into the pages, so we are definitely going to need that tweaked a bit still, just wanted to add in a note about it when people go to use the inventory more.  

At least the left/right buttons work on the item details page right now, so if you manage to get really deep in your inventory and click on an item, you can still browse through them fairly easy.  I'll try get the inventory page to come back to the last one you were on, that alone will make a big difference.  [/p]

notes.title: New CPS (clicks-per-second) Indicator
notes.content:
[p]Hey small update, I added a clicks-per-second feature on the main screen.  Since I set up the autoclicker to go slightly faster with each unique item you own I figured it would be good to have a gauge on the screen where you can see exactly how fast it's going, or if you click at the same time, just a way to measure your speed.  

I set it up so if you click on it, it stops calculating in case it had a performance impact on your clicking speed, you have the choice to have it on or not.  Helpful also to see if lower framerates have slower speeds!  

With 324 uniques (I think I'm only missing a couple) my AC runs at 148 CPS at 60 FPS and 110 CPS at 30 FPS.  Pretty big differences in speed so I'm glad I set this up, this was badly needed!  

More stuff coming soon just wanted to point out how this works!  Cheers!
  [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45270362/24590d1e9a1dd742eefc3966f8f5594e081e0062.png"][/img][/p]

notes.title: v1.342 Patch Notes
notes.content:
[list][*][p]Game now launches into English on 1st-time launch, previously it was loading Bulgarian until you chose another language in the settings (which would stay).  It now saves the language files on first time bootup.  [/p][/*][*][p]Optimized cloud saving saving logic, previously it was saving every 500 clicks but now:

- Up to 100 clicks of a session, saves every 10 clicks
- Then up to 500 clicks of a session, it saves every 100 clicks
- Then up to 2000 clicks in a session, it saves every 500 clicks
- Then after that, it saves every 2000 clicks

This way if you open it up for the first time or just click a little bit, it's likely going to save that progress but if you are clicking fast with the auto-clicker then it will shift into a mode where it's likely saving at a decent pace.  Just wanted to leave a note with the exact saving points.[/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: JAMs Season 3!!
notes.content:
Hey everyone!  

Well I'm back from my trip and got us caught up on new items, and I was thinking of altering the system in such a way that would accommodate sporadic trips (as I have another one coming up in a month or so anyway) so here is what I have come up with as a solution.  I'll just leave them in the drop pool for a longer period of time, still cycle them out but if I fall a few days behind it would barely be noticeable to people if there were a lot of different items dropping.  

Previously I was cycling them out every 5 days, I think a number as high as 30 days/items would be pretty reasonable to have as a common drop pool, any more than that would take awhile to get the newer items.  And since I switched it to season 2 after fixing things and changing the distribution/timing last time, I figured it was a good time to call this season 3.  It should be a lot easier for everyone to stay up to date and would give me much better flexibility to work on the actual game itself, it should work out great this way.  

And my favorite bit of good news is that [b]Steam has fixed the auto-stack feature for timed drop items[/b]!!  I had them configured to do so and when I was on my trip they just started auto-stacking on their own and you will probably notice a lot of other games have their items auto-stacking recently now too.  If you stack your items manually once now you won't have to do it again, but I'll still try to get item stacking functionality built into the app at some point.

Thanks for playing and lots of stuff coming down the pipeline in the coming months! :)

notes.title: Inventory screen!
notes.content:
Hey!!

I've been tinkering away with building this inventory screen, it was pretty complicated as Unity doesn't support GIFs out of the box, and I wanted it to download the images only for the ones you own, so I don't have to keep patching in the new items every time.  

This was a bit of a journey!  It downloads them and brings them up from local storage if they are already downloaded, but it will load them all up every time you enter the inventory screen.  I had it working where the images were loaded much faster, but the program goes into a 'not responding' state as it thinks too hard and overloads the thread, the way it is set up currently it does them one at a time slowly and just gets it done --- I like it this way since you can still navigate away once it's started to load.  

Since we are decoding the gifs and playing them back, the system is basically breaking them apart into individual frames, and since we have tons of frames and if you have lots of items, your RAM usage might get incredibly high during the loading of that screen currently.  This situation may not scale well as we keep adding items, so I might even make a toggle switch for different approaches of how the inventory screen loads or behaves, but for people with just a few items it's not a big deal, and when you navigate away from that page, it unloads all the memory so I think it's better that we don't have the images preloaded if it's that nuts on the memory already.  

I will make pages with the details and tools of the items and I still need to do the tooltips, but lets just see how this goes so far!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45270362/0de28c020fdafa5176682110bf27e4462656fada.png[/img]

More features coming soon!  Starting to get the hang of it!

notes.title: Controller Support
notes.content:
Hey!  Switched to the newer Unity "Input System" and added some basic controller support for navigating the menus, and made it so that if you have the autoclicker and it's disabled you can autofire on the main screen at the same rate it would go at with it on.  Since it is an active use thing versus an idle feature I could actually make it go faster, I was just setting it up for now, can sort out the details later.

[i]I'll also add a toggle feature to disable gamepad support, I can imagine situations where you might not want it.[/i]

I have the settings only affected on the settings page still, and [b]Start[/b] changes the Resolution, [b]Select[/b] toggles the FPS, [b]B[/b] toggles Autoclick. and the D-Pad, Right Stick, and shoulder buttons can be used for navigating around to the different pages.

notes.title: Keyboard Navigation + AutoClicker Bonus Speed
notes.content:
Hey in this build I added some basic keyboard controls for navigation.  This should make it easy to get to the settings screen using the arrow key to the right, and then [u]on the settings screen[/u] you can press [b]"R"[/b] for resolution, and in theory that should begin to flip through some of the options I have in there.  I hope this corrects everyone's screen sizes!

You can also press [b]"A"[/b] [u]on the settings menu[/u] to toggle the autoclicker, and [b]"F"[/b] toggles the FPS.  Not sure why it only changes between 2 different FPS's at a time, but it almost works better this way imo flipping between 5 and 90 fps for example.  

Also I recently put in a change where the autoclicker will click faster depending on how many JAMs you have in your inventory.  Yes, I finally figured out how to scan the inventory so on the info panel you will see your unique/total numbers.  I tried to figure out a quick solution and it basically shaves a tiny bit off the click interval with each additional one, so from 0.01s clicks taking off 0.00001s each additional, so having ~124 of them is a 0.00124 reduction so 0.00876s click speed in that example.  I think that number works for now as it only allows for 1000 items total so in theory over time it should just get faster and faster.  

Steam cloud click saving is also changed to save more frequently but then less frequently depending on how many clicks are in that session.  So less people should experience missed clicks now in lower numbers but then as you cruise along at high speed it saves less frequently.

notes.title: Cleaning Up The Market A Bit
notes.content:
Hey!  I'm still here jammin' away every day, in one aspect or another!  

You may have noticed awhile back that somehow all the items became messed up and variants became created.  That was and is still pretty frustrating to look at, but they are still items and we will fix them or make a system to convert them back into marketable versions, but there are not supposed to be more than 1 listing of each item anyway so at least temporarily, everything up to (ironically) "Steamy" was broken.  

The tags are not on the items themselves, they were on the item generator and apparently those tags get sent into the item descriptions of what it generates, and the tags were there since the beginning but were not visible because I had not set up the inventory sorting / localization stuff, the moment I did that everything went haywire.  

[i]Just removing marketability of them, they are still tradeable, it's just the descriptions that got messed up.[/i]

I have not missed a day creating new items though, and there should be enough still left in the market so there is something to look at, it's not the end of the world here just letting you all know what I am trying here.  I am not abandoning the designs, we are just sort of shelving them for a sec.  When we have a solution it's just going to be a 1 for 1 swap to get back into a marketable version, ideally.

I recommend stacking them, they actually stack to the different versions really neat-and-tidy-like.  

https://github.com/steamnerds/userscripts
^ this is the script that everyone on Steam uses to stack items with.  it works great, if you are not familiar with it, it requires using an API key and the google chrome web console.  It's only for stacking and unstacking items, I'll have these types of features in the game itself at some point.  You can also just transfer the items to an alt account to clean up in the meantime.

The game gives a lot of items so it's almost necessary, I literally just got stunned when the items split all apart like that so this is a way to at least have a super clean experience for all new players who are seeing my insane wall of videos on Bluesky, then looking at the actual game itself and --- it's pretty much a mess --- yea.., but I plan on working at this project forever so I just want things to be as clean and tidy as possible!  Please just stack up the old ones and we will deal with them later so I can focus on actually learning how the editor works instead of how to solve this bizarre problem.  So glad they were all free items, people would be so mad if they had to buy all those!  The 1st DLC set got roasted too, but again it's just a temporary solution as different versions of these items are ridiculous to be on the market.

Just like I even said in the banjo song on the store page I didn't want anything to be broken, and then immediately the whole market like explodes, but I can count 25 items since then so the market will hopefully function just as well as it did the day everything broke in the first place.  

Anyways thanks for hanging out with me and my bizarre Steam game adventure, Season 1 sure has been an adventure for me and I'm looking forward to iterate on what have going on so far.  I know it doesn't really make a lot of sense, but I think it's going pretty well.  If it wasn't for the item description disaster I'd say things were going perfect.  

It may take a bit for the changes to completely take effect, don't buy anything thinking it's a last minute chance to get one, they are plentiful it's just different versions of the same items appeared.

notes.title: Added Item Tags + Localization
notes.content:
Hey quick update:

I added localization for all languages (hooray!) in the inventory section, so now our items won't say "Unique" in front of them anymore, but this may have caused... The names of existing ones to change, and since they already exist we have to just move forward with it.  So in the markets, there are probably going to be some duplicated listings as the names of things are what determines how the listing pages work, but if it comes down to it I'll make a box where you can just swap a "Unique" one for a "V2" of the same item (or just hang onto the Unique ones as unintentional collectors items ːbgt_laughterː).  But seriously though I wish I had realized this would have happened, I would have swapped the whole set at once, but I like my 1-item-a-day thing so.. yea I think it could be just as easy to make a button that just fixes the whole inventory at once, really, so don't panic if you have concerns over the potentially confusing inventory, I'll figure out a solution for it!

And the item of the day is Steamy, so ironically we have Steamy issues on Steamy day, and there are potentially a couple different versions of it out there.  I think we have smoothened out the issue though pretty quick!  Apparently the tags on an item generator go into the items within, and also go into the description.
